question: In MS-Word, a number printed above the base line is called ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**superscript**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A number printed above the base line in MS-Word is referred to as a **superscript**.
 
• Superscripts are often used in mathematical expressions, chemical formulas, and for footnotes or endnotes in documents.
 
• To apply superscript formatting in MS-Word, you can use the shortcut key **Ctrl + Shift + +** or use the Superscript button in the Font group on the Home tab.
 
• Examples of superscripts include 2ⁿd, x², and H₂O where the "2" is in a smaller, raised font above the baseline.
 
• Superscripts are different from subscripts, which are printed below the baseline and are used for different purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• MS-Word offers various text formatting options, including bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, subscript, and superscript.
 
• Formatting text can enhance the readability and presentation of your document.
 
• Using the correct formatting options ensures that your document is clear and professional.
